_readme: THE APP'S OWN DEPRECIATION RATES — the floor every country falls back to (item 4.78).
🔴 THESE ARE NOT ANY COUNTRY'S Depreciation Rates AND MUST NEVER BE PRESENTED AS ONE. They are
the six figures the Three-Way Forecast has shipped with since it was built, and they
are a guess: Vehicles is 20% where New Zealand's IRD gives 50% diminishing value for a
passenger vehicle. That gap is the whole reason item 4.78 exists. Everything here is
tagged `app default` on screen, in exactly those words, so nobody reads it as sourced.
WHY THE NUMBERS LIVE HERE RATHER THAN ONLY IN THE SCREEN. They were declared twice —
ASSET_SPECS in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue (percentages) and the engine's own
defaults in server/report/threeWayForecastModel.js (decimals). A cascading store needs a
third reading of the same six numbers, and three copies is two too many.
tests/unit/depreciationRates.test.js pins this file against the ENGINE's defaults, which are the
ones that actually compute a forecast, so the three can no longer drift apart.
🔴 RATES ARE DECIMALS, 0..1 — 50% is 0.5, never 50. That is the engine's own convention
(threeWayForecastModel assetSchedule multiplies by it directly) and the backend's
convention everywhere else (server/utils/propertyTaxRules.js). The intake SCREEN works
in percentages and converts; the store never does.
`method` is `dv` (diminishing value) for all six because that is what the engine does —
it depreciates the reducing book value, not the original cost. A `sl` rate cannot be
stored here for the same reason: nothing would read it.
`source` is null on every entry, and that is the point. A rate with no source document
is an app default; a rate WITH one came from a tax document a firm manager approved.
The screen tells them apart by exactly this field.
